recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the work group wants a new broader policy on non-standard comment-like properties in JSON instances.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core JSON-page issue asking to clarify that the specification's pseudo-JSON examples may use // comments, but // is JavaScript syntax and comments are not allowed in JSON files or instances; a _comment property might be ignored by some processors but would not be valid.
initial_application: Git commit f615f53824fcb9432db703108c72399b1c9a83c1, matching Jira's svn revision 14249 comment, changed source/json.html to state that // is legal in Javascript but not JSON and comments are invalid in JSON instances regardless of whether applications ignore them.
additional_context: source/json.html is active build content via publish.ini. A later 2025 commit corrected the normative capitalization to SHALL NOT. Older JSON-comment issues show historical fhir_comments/comment support was removed or superseded, and 2018 FHIR-I minutes align with the Persuasive with Modification vote. Exact community searches found no conflicting FHIR-17005 discussion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current JSON page already conveys the requested rule, and adding separate _comment prose would be redundant next to the existing SHALL NOT statement.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published issue requested examples for the then-existing fhir_comments JSON convention; it explains historical comment support but predates its removal.
Resolved - No Change ITS issue records the later conclusion that comments are no longer supported in FHIR.
